package_info.why_malicious: The report is a high-level threat intelligence summary and does not provide specific package-level details or code samples. It discusses ransomware families and their deployment via various malware, but does not analyze a particular software package or provide code.

behavioral_signatures: Phishing email delivery of malware droppers (e.g., Emotet, Qakbot, Dridex, IcedID)
Initial access malware establishing persistence and downloading ransomware payloads
Lateral movement using legitimate tools (e.g., Cobalt Strike, RDP exploitation)
Data exfiltration prior to ransomware deployment (double/triple extortion)
Ransomware encryption of files and display of ransom notes
file_indicators: Presence of known ransomware payloads (e.g., XingLocker, Mount Locker, REvil, Ryuk, Dridex, Qakbot, Emotet)
Unusual executable files dropped in user directories
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known C2 infrastructure associated with ransomware groups
Connections to suspicious or newly registered domains
Use of legitimate cloud storage or file sharing services for data exfiltration
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for phishing emails containing malicious attachments or links, especially those delivering known malware droppers. Detect unusual process creation and privilege escalation, especially involving tools like Cobalt Strike or RDP. Watch for outbound network connections to known malicious infrastructure and for the creation of ransom note files or mass file encryption activity. Use threat intelligence feeds to correlate observed indicators with known ransomware campaigns.
